clue.text: Shop has dainty cape returned

parts.note: dainty means delicate, fine and fragile

indicators.note: returned means the word for the cape is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A shop is said to stock a dainty cape that came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NESS into SSEN, which follows DELICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a store selling prepared foods, cooked meats and cheeses.

clue.text: Popular book among detectives — give it up !

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells us to read the whole assembly from the bottom upwards
among means the book's word goes inside the detectives' letters

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A popular book about detectives, and an exasperated plea to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts TOME inside CID to make CITOMED; 'give it up' then reverses all of it, which in a down entry reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotic language is that of the common people, so it is popular in the old sense of belonging to ordinary folk.

clue.text: Cut made, by cricket beginner, in a way

indicators.note: in means the cricket letter sits inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way

indicators.note: beginner means only the opening letter of cricket is used

explanation.surface: A cut made by a novice cricketer, somewhere along a lane.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to cut it open with a small blade.

clue.text: Friar, appears to feel, concern about me getting settled

indicators.note: about means the word for concern goes round the other pieces

parts.note: care means concern or worry
taken as written
lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means settled or alighted

explanation.surface: A friar seems to feel worried about someone settling in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ME and LIT inside CARE, splitting it as CAR...E. The clue as printed has no commas: 'appears to feel' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmelites are members of a mendicant order, the White Friars, founded on Mount Carmel.

clue.text: River vessel upset by youth leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the vessel's word is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or vessel for liquids

indicators.note: leader means only the opening letter of youth is used

explanation.surface: A boat on a river capsized by the head of a youth group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns VAT into TAV; the Tavy is a river on Dartmoor in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tavy is a Devon waterway flowing past Tavistock into the Tamar.

clue.text: Like a relative of R.L.S., yet is different

indicators.note: different means these letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: the initials taken as their three letters

explanation.surface: Someone resembles a kinsman of Robert Louis Stevenson, yet is unlike him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges RLS, YET and IS; R.L.S. is Robert Louis Stevenson, which tempts a solver towards a literary relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisterly means behaving as a female sibling would.

clue.text: Score made by player ?

explanation.surface: A score contributed by one of the players.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run added to the total that no batsman hits; on a film set an extra is a minor actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is both a run credited to a cricket side without a stroke and a performer hired for a crowd scene.

clue.text: Express dissatisfaction with a break in the service

indicators.note: break in means the single letter breaks into the service's word

parts.note: Complin, or Compline, is the last church service of the day

explanation.surface: Grumbling about an interruption in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break in' puts A into COMPLIN, between L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to voice a grievance.

clue.text: Offer old coins to queen

parts.note: ten pennies in pre-decimal British money were written 10d, read as TEN D
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone offers some old money to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British pence were abbreviated d, so ten old pennies is TEN D.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to present a bid or payment formally.

clue.text: Trees from the island woods

parts.note: the Isle of Man is often just the island in crosswords
groves are small woods

explanation.surface: Trees taken from the woods of some island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are tropical coastal shrubs and timber growing in salt water.

clue.text: Left back gets point of the metaphor

indicators.note: back means the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A footballer's left back gets the point of a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left back' reads like the football position; 'back' turns PORT into TROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, and a metaphor is the standard example.

clue.text: Old city just fails to achieve optimum rating

indicators.note: falling just short means the final letter is not reached

parts.note: the best is the top rating, the optimum

explanation.surface: An ancient city narrowly misses being rated the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just fails to achieve' drops the last letter of THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a great ancient capital in Egypt, and also a city of Greek legend.

clue.text: Absconded with document about soldiers' quarters, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the document's word goes round the quarters

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a camp is one example of where soldiers are housed

explanation.surface: Someone ran off with papers about army barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CAMP inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, to make off.

clue.text: Composer was happy as, a sand-boy?

definitions.text: Composer was happy as, a sand-boy?

parts.words: Composer was happy as, a sand-boy?
parts.note: the saying 'happy as a sandboy' is read as the boy of George Sand, the French novelist whose lover was a Polish pianist-composer

explanation.surface: A composer was as contented as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy as a sandboy' is a British phrase for very cheerful; the novelist George Sand lived with this Polish composer for nine years. The page prints no comma after 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin, the Polish composer, was George Sand's partner, her 'Sand boy'.

clue.text: Shrub reset by dear Noel

indicators.note: reset means the letters are set again in a new order

explanation.surface: A bush replanted by someone called Noel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' rearranges DEAR and NOEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen bush with pink or white flowers.

clue.text: What a pity Rita confounded him !

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of regret

indicators.note: confounded means the letters of Rita are mixed up

explanation.surface: Rita has thoroughly confused some poor man, more's the pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' turns RITA into TAIR; 'him' defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a Scottish male given name, so a man can be referred to as 'him'.

clue.text: (No way to get) one kind of boundary

explanation.surface: A fence that admits nobody is one sort of boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: To stonewall is to block or obstruct, giving no way through; a stone wall is also a field boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstruction that lets nothing pass, and a wall of stones marks a field's edge.

clue.text: A criterion in a way — and a different way

parts.note: St, street, is a way
Rd, road, is another kind of way

explanation.surface: A test measured one way and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, AND, A and RD run together in order; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a benchmark used to judge quality.

clue.text: Risks increasing figure at board meeting ?

definitions.text: Risks increasing figure at board meeting

parts.words: Risks increasing figure at board meeting
parts.note: the board is the dining table, and the figure is the waistline, so this is someone who eats too much at a meal

explanation.surface: A company director takes chances that push up the numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is the old word for a table spread with food (as in bed and board), and 'figure' is one's shape, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has too much at table puts on weight.

clue.text: Perhaps a native story — eastern sort

indicators.note: sort as a verb means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps a local folk tale of an Eastern kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges STORY and E; a 'native' is an oyster raised in British beds, as at Whitstable.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are oysters bred in British waters, so a native is an example of the shellfish.

clue.text: Canons get fired ?

explanation.surface: Clerics are sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A canon in music is a round, sung in overlapping parts; rounds are also shots fired from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical canons are part-songs repeating the same tune, and ammunition units are discharged from guns.

clue.text: What a bet has that a better hasn't-put your shirt on it ?

definitions.text: What a bet has that a better hasn't-put your shirt on it

parts.words: What a bet has that a better hasn't-put your shirt on it
parts.note: the word bet contains one T where better has two, and that letter description is also a vest you can wear

explanation.surface: Gambling advice: back it with everything you own.
explanation.walkthrough: To put your shirt on something is to stake everything on it; here the 'shirt' is the garment named by 'single T'.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest or athletic shirt.

clue.text: Prison offence connected with key duplication

indicators.note: duplication means the joined pieces are written twice

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A gaol offence involving copying keys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a musical key, not one for a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a maximum-security penitentiary in New York State.

clue.text: Type-writer ?

explanation.surface: A typewriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Style means type or kind; a style (stylus) is also a pointed writing instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is a manner or kind, and a style was the pointed tool used to write on wax tablets.

clue.text: Female's male ?

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A woman's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a man's name as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman is a masculine given name, so a man so called is a male.

clue.text: Many eager to see the giant

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, taken as many
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: Lots of people are keen to see the giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giants of British legend whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Magog is one of the two legendary colossi, with Gog, guarding the City of London.

clue.text: Scrutinize bills up North

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the bills' letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: acs are accounts, which are bills

explanation.surface: Checking bills up in the North of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ACS into SCA in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine closely.

clue.text: Time to fight ?

explanation.surface: The bell rings for the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is often called the enemy, as in 'time is the enemy'; and an enemy is someone you fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is the proverbial foe of everyone, and a foe is an opponent in battle.

clue.text: Port for Michael, perhaps

explanation.surface: A port wine served to Michael.
explanation.walkthrough: Archangel (Arkhangelsk) is a Russian port on the White Sea; Michael is an angel of the highest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkhangelsk is a northern Russian harbour city, and Michael is one of the chief angels.

clue.text: Perhaps a link with a very influential member ?

explanation.surface: A connection with a powerful person.
explanation.walkthrough: A link was a torch carried to light people through dark streets, so it gave a guiding flame; a leading light is also a prominent figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A link-boy's torch went before walkers to show the path, and a prominent person guides others.
